answer: A newcomer must reserve one meadow plot on a public cadastral map, cut a nine-layer shale wafer, and lock 0.72 POA against it before any payout. They etch a 240-character origin fable whose hash binds plot index plus deposit, so spare machines cannot reuse another plot's color. Layers are witnessed 150 seconds apart and never in parallel. Three auditors peel random layers, rebuild the fable hash, and match the cadastral Merkle leaf to the live tip. A mismatched layer costs 0.04 POA. Shared fable prefixes or early layers slash both deposits 60 percent and seal that plot for 5 epochs.
